Background
Etta and Claribel Cone were prominent art collectors who developed a close relationship with Henri Matisse over several decades. Their friendship began in 1906, and Etta Cone became one of Matisse's most loyal patrons. After Claribel's death in 1929, Etta continued to build their collection and maintained her correspondence with Matisse.
The Commission
In 1930, during Matisse's visit to the United States, Etta Cone commissioned him to create a portrait of Claribel. This portrait was intended to serve as a tribute to her sister and was part of Etta's efforts to document and celebrate their extensive art collection, which included many works by Matisse himself.
